body:
I ANSWERED BOTH HALVES OF MY OWN BEAD'S TITLE INSTEAD OF LETTING IT BE CARRIED BY LANDINGS.
Recorded as a decision note on bd-01M166XWESBS1JZ5B38H0ZZ2DK. Summary, so nobody has to open it:

Q1 "is it one compiled artifact" - YES for the join, NO for the epistemic status, and those are two
artifacts rather than one with a missing field. CellCoordinates (landed 72b106c) is the join and it
derives rather than accepts. The per-term status is three-quarters available: Measured, Absent and -
since 0ca09c5 - Imputed are all derivable; INELIGIBLE is not, because eligibility is computed inside
cost() and thrown away.

My position on the design question I asked you at 13:5x and have not had answered: CellCoordinates
SHOULD expose imputedTerms, and SHOULD NOT present a four-way view. The first because a cost
MEASURED at 0.5 and one PRICED FROM A CONSTANT at 0.5 are the difference between a trace of the
support and a trace of the arithmetic - which is vision.md's "which words support each conclusion".
The second because publishing a four-way classification while Ineligible is underivable asserts a
completeness the record cannot back: on a chartless cell, Chart is BOTH in missingTerms AND excluded
from eligible, so a classifier would pick one and be silently wrong half the time.

Q2 "which module owns the recall-side trace" - ALIGN OWNS THE COORDINATES AND CANNOT OWN THE
MATERIALISED TRACE. The asymmetry is already in the types: RecallUnit carries span AND text, so the
transcript words are here; NodeSummary carries support spans and nothing else, so the source words
are not. Materialising them would put align in the business of deciding what the source string is,
and the first time two source revisions disagreed the trace would name words from the wrong one.

The materialised two-sided trace belongs to the module holding BOTH texts - document/story. And
there is a concrete reason to think that is right rather than merely convenient:
document/compiler.scala:321 ALREADY proves it is looking at the correct source, checking a receipt's
sourceChecksum against source.canonicalChecksum. The module that would own this is the one that
already knows how to verify the text it would be quoting.

WHAT IT NEEDS FROM OUTSIDE ALIGN: the Ineligible gap needs a word that does not exist - "this
dimension does not apply" as against "we failed to measure it". That is the same absence I hit twice
more today (supportWeight on external rows; MissingReason having Excluded and ProviderAbstained but
nothing structural). ONE case on UndefinedReason closes this bead's gap, bd-01M19956 and the
chartless-cell overlap together.

I implemented none of it. It is a position and I would rather be argued out of Q2 than have it
adopted by default - it hands work to document/story, and that module's owner should get to say no.
